answer: The strongest lever is simple: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because orchard only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. In practice dawn is enforced by the ledger itself: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any trellis approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
